text:
incident-bot: [PAGER] hosted-api us-east-1 queue spike detected — queue_depth p95=12,300, p99 latency=18.2s, request timeouts increasing. Paging @anna_oncall, @lucy_sre, @mike_infra. Auto-escalation in 2m.

anna_oncall: I'm on it. Pulling up the dashboard and logs. Is this from one tenant or multi-tenant?

mike_infra: quick hit: provisioner is failing some instance creations — seeing quota errors from cloud provider. grabbing logs now.

mike_infra: ```
ERROR 2024-04-12T22:34:12Z provisioner: CreateInstance failed: QuotaExceeded: limit 40 GPUs reached for project X
ProvisionRequest{req_id=aa12, desired=5, created=2, failed=3}
```

lucy_sre: running runbook step 3 (spike handling). Priorities: 1) stop noisy clients if obvious, 2) reduce concurrency/batch size, 3) enable model-fallback routing to smaller-quantized variant, 4) escalate quota. Implementing 2 & 3 now.

dev-exec: started a targeted route change for top 8 high-QPS API keys to redirect to dedicated-capacity pool with lower-cost model variant (canary). Doing in small increments.

ops-bot: autoscaler attempted 12 VM creations at 22:34:09Z. Results: 8 succeeded, 4 failed. Fail messages aggregated: [QuotaExceeded, RateLimitExceeded]. Action: manual retry blocked by quota.

paul_prod: Customer telemetry — several high-volume apps are returning 504s. Top impacted: tenant-corp (5% errors last 5m), demo-bot (3%). We should include a customer impact note for SRE->CS handoff.

anna_oncall: mitigation actions executed: - batching reduced from 64 -> 16 for hosted endpoints (good immediate CPU mem drop) - disabled prefix caching for long-running streams to reduce KV pressure - enabled local per-API-key throttles at 100rps for noisy keys - enabled fallback routing to quantized-x4 model for best-effort low-cost path. Early effect: p99 dropped to ~6s for redirected traffic; overall queue still trending up.

mike_infra: opening emergency quota request with cloud support and filing ticket with billing team. We'll also spin up spare nodes in reserved pool (if available) to relieve immediate pressure. If reserved pool isn't sufficient, we have to shed or degrade more aggressively.

lucy_sre: I'm going to exec runbook snippet: ```
# runbook: reduce concurrency and prefer fallback
POST /config/reload
{"max_concurrency": 8, "default_batch_size": 16, "fallback_percent": 30}
```

dev-exec: can confirm route switch logs — traffic for top keys now 40% on dedicated fallback-canary, 60% on hosted. Dedicated pool CPU at 72% and handling fine.

paul_prod: CS alert prepared: short note to tenants affected explaining increased latencies and mitigations in-flight. Suggest posting status page update.

sarah_support: posting status update to status.redwood.ai: "Experiencing elevated latencies and timeouts in us-east-1; mitigation steps underway; will update in 15 minutes." Also opening inbound ticket list for tenants with >1% error rate.

ops-bot: manual capacity action: reserved-pool spin-up initiated by @mike_infra. Provisioner log: attempted to allocate 6 reserved nodes — 4 allocated, 2 pending due to API quotas.

anna_oncall: current assessment: partial mitigation achieved via routing + throttles, p99 improved for canaryed traffic, but global p99 still ~9s and queue length slowly increasing. Hypothesis: combination of sudden warm-start traffic from a large client plus provisioner quota limits causing slow replenish.

lucy_sre: I'll take the night handoff in 30m. Actions to follow in handoff note: 1) continue quota escalation, 2) maintain routing to dedicated pool for top clients, 3) consider temporary global rate limiter at 2500 rps if queue grows >15k, 4) collect heap/profile from serving runtime for slow tokens. Runbook link: https://internal/runbooks/spikes#step3.

anna_oncall: documented runbook steps taken in incident doc, adding logs and commands run. Timeline: 22:34 initial pager -> 22:40 throttles & batch reductions -> 22:46 route canary -> 22:52 reserved pool partial fill.

mike_infra: cloud support replied: quota escalation requested, ETA 2-4 hours. They've unlocked 2 GPUs immediately (temporary). We can do a hot-redeploy to use them but it will take ~7 minutes to have capacity online. Initiating now.

dev-exec: redeploy to pick up new nodes started: command: `infra deploy --region us-east-1 --pool reserved-emergency` — watching logs.

ops-bot: deploy stage: SUCCESS after 6m 12s. New capacity shows in cluster: +6 GPUs. Autoscaler state stable.

paul_prod: after deploy/pinning more traffic to reserved pool, visible improvement: p99 -> 4.2s overall, queue depth plateaued and beginning to shrink. Customer error rates trending down. Recommend marking incident as mitigated but continue monitoring for 1h.

sarah_support: I've messaged impacted tenants with update and ETA for full resolution. Will coordinate any postmortem comms.

lucy_sre: taking handoff now. Will maintain close watch for next hour and then transition to SEV review. Root cause hypothesis recorded: sudden sustained burst + provisioning quota prevented autoscaler from restoring desired capacity quickly, fallback coverage partially insufficient because only 30% of traffic routed at first. Postmortem actions to propose: increase fallback ramp %, pre-warm common tenants in reserved pools, and automate quota prechecks.

anna_oncall: ack, thanks team. Leaving notes and transferring on-call to @lucy_sre. Closing live mitigation thread; keeping incident channel open for follow-up. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: Incident status: TRIAGED -> MITIGATED. Monitor window: 60m. Metrics to watch: queue_depth, p99_latency, provisioner_failures.

lucy_sre: will open a postmortem ticket and assign owners for the three follow-ups. Thanks all.
